title: Homeowner Service Contracts — Number of Contracts a Customer May Hold
content:
**Clause.** A customer may hold any number of Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts, one for each distinct property they own and occupy as a residence. How many contracts one property may carry is governed by the one-contract-per-property rule for Homeowner Service Contracts.

**Restated.** There is no maximum on the number of Homeowner Service Contracts one customer holds. The count is set by properties, not by the customer: each contract belongs to one distinct property that the customer owns and occupies as a residence.

| Question | Answer under this clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a per-customer limit on Homeowner Service Contracts? | No limit is set. |
| What does each contract attach to? | One distinct property the customer owns and occupies as a residence. |
| Does this clause decide how many contracts one property may carry? | No; that is governed by the one-contract-per-property rule. |

*Illustration, hypothetical:* a homeowner who owns and occupies two distinct residences may hold one Homeowner Service Contract on each, so two contracts in all.
